On the next screen you will draw or upload a Coarse Boundary Polygon for your project.
This polygon should contain your entire region of interest. GEM will automatically determine the exact boundary by buffering the coastline found within the coarse polygon.
Nothing outside this coarse polygon will be included in the analysis. You can also define areas to be excluded from analysis or Sub-Regions to be treated separately during analysis.

The CRAs may take some effort to compile for your region, and should be shape files containing square (pixel-aligned) plots 70-85 meters per side that contain examples of your different classification areas (Mangrove, Not Mangrove, Water etc). In addition, there must be an attribute that gives the name for the class of each plot, and another numeric attribute that gives a number associated with the class for each plot. 

The data looks something like this: 

                    | Name               | Value 
-----------------------------------------------------------

[polygon b] | Mangrove        | 1 
[polygon c] | Mangrove        | 1 
[polygon d] | Mangrove        | 1 
[polygon e] | Not Mangrove | 2 
[polygon g] | Not Mangrove | 2 
[polygon h] | Not Mangrove | 2

On the next screen you will assess whether your imagery is fit for purpose and ready to be classified.
Your 4 composites (contemporary and historical, for both highest observed tide (HOT) and lowest observed tide (LOT)) are fit for purpose if:
• There is visible difference in tide levels between high and low tide for both contemporary and historical composites.
• Look out for exposed tidal flats in the LOT composite, if any are present these should be smaller or fully inundated by the incoming tide in the HOT composite.
• The coastline may have shifted inland slightly in the HOT composite.
• Exposed areas of mudflats in between mangroves may appear more damp or even as water in the HOT composite.

• Water in river channels and around estuaries may be a darker blue in the HOT composite (indicating deeper water), whilst a lighter grainier blue in the LOT composite (due to turbid water that is holding more coastal sediment).
• There are no missing pixels present (a very small number of missing pixels in places where mangroves are unlikely to be is ok).
